meta.real_gap_found_and_fixed: run_campaign() acquires the running lease via campaign.set_mission(mid, status="running") before calling launch_provider(); if the process is killed before launch_provider() returns, the mission is left permanently at status="running" on disk -- next_mission() only selects "pending" rows and "running" is not in _SETTLED_DEP_STATUSES, so the mission and anything depending on it are wedged forever. Same crash-mid-run family as F011 but at the campaign-mission level.

Recovery is unconditional on any "running" mission at start-of-run, correct under the single-active-writer guarantee (rule 1) but would be unsafe if a second concurrent writer ever violated that guarantee (a distinct fault, F020).

meta.fix: Added campaign_state.JournalCorrupted(RuntimeError), raised by verify_events() for both a truncated/unparseable line and a hash/prev_hash mismatch. run_campaign() now calls campaign.verify_events() FIRST, before _recover_orphaned_leases/reconstruct_progress touch anything -- on JournalCorrupted it returns {campaign_state: WAITING_HUMAN, reason_code: RECOVERY_REQUIRED} immediately with zero mutation of events.jsonl or missions.jsonl.
meta.real_gap_found_and_fixed: Campaign.event() appends via write()+flush()+fsync(); a real crash between write() and fsync completing can leave the trailing line truncated/unparseable. factoryctl.load_jsonl() raised a bare RuntimeError for that line, propagating UNCAUGHT out of verify_events() -> reconstruct_progress() -> run_campaign(), crashing the orchestrator with a raw traceback and never recording WAITING_HUMAN -- the campaign was permanently stuck but nothing said so. Order §5.3 forbids self-healing here ("Aucune reprise auto sur journal tronqué / hash-chain invalide / état ambigu"): correct behavior is campaign_state=WAITING_HUMAN + reason_code=RECOVERY_REQUIRED, unlike F011/F012's legitimate self-healing.
meta.real_limitation: Simulates the crash by writing a real events.jsonl via Campaign.event() then severing the trailing line's characters directly (the real shape a torn write leaves), rather than literally SIGKILLing the process mid-write() syscall. The hash-chain-tamper variant is F014's shape and is exercised by this same fix/test, but F014 keeps its own dedicated tranche/test rather than being silently claimed done by proxy.

meta.fix: Added Campaign.check_no_rollback(): compares the current events.jsonl event_count against the last persisted progress.json snapshot's event_count; raises JournalCorrupted if it shrank. run_campaign() now calls campaign.check_no_rollback() immediately after verify_events(), inside the same try/except JournalCorrupted block, before _recover_orphaned_leases/reconstruct_progress touch anything.
meta.real_gap_found_and_fixed: verify_events() only checks that the CURRENT events.jsonl is internally self-consistent (per-line hash + prev_hash chain); it says nothing about whether the file has been silently replaced by an earlier, shorter but still individually hash-valid PREFIX of itself. Campaign.event() only ever appends, so event_count can never legitimately shrink between two reconstructions -- but reconstruct_progress() unconditionally overwrote progress.json with whatever the current (possibly rolled-back) chain reconstructs to, with zero comparison against the previously-persisted snapshot, silently erasing evidence that later events (e.g. a mission's done event) ever happened.
meta.real_limitation: Simulates the rollback by writing a real events.jsonl via Campaign.event() then replacing it with an exact prefix of its own lines (the real shape a restored-backup or truncate-then-continue attack leaves, since no rehashing is needed for a prefix) rather than a live attacker process. Detects the corruption only ACROSS two separate run_campaign()/reconstruct_progress() invocations (comparing to the last persisted progress.json) -- a rollback that occurs and is overwritten again within a single run_campaign() call before progress.json is ever read back is out of this check's scope, since progress.json is only read once per invocation.
